title: Greer as the band's street-smart member
summary: He knew night life better than Duke and the boys.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, tell me this, when you were -- were you the one in the band that had the most kind of like know-how in terms of how -- the corners to get around?

Yeah, I was the one. You know, it was a brand new whole world for Duke and the boys, it was a brand new world. They didn't know that stuff. But I was always involved in it from time beginning. I was involved in night life. I recorded. I was there. So I just picked up fast on all that stuff. And, you know, it was always looking for a curve, man I was looking for a curve.
You see, me and Fats and all the guys, and all of us, we were -- Willie 'the Lion' --, we were always looking for a curve, what we call a curve. We didn't miss nothing.
We didn't miss nothing. We were looking for the curve and we worked for each other. We were a closely knit bunch of guys.
